title: Native C model, per-edge corpus, refinement records, metrics

predictions.claim: Native and .mjs agree on 100% of the refuter's candidates. Operationalized: for every M0 law, every candidate holon.refute.candidates yields (the whole candidate space, not stopped at the first hit), every claim term (both sides and every subterm, as holon.refute evaluates them) gives the same value on the native C model (an ELF binary, run with no node or bend reachable) and on the .mjs model, with evaluation errors compared as a class; results/M2/native.json records the same counts. A recorded fallback to .mjs is a miss of this prediction.

Per codec edge: 2,000 grammar samples, all boundary values, all witnesses. Operationalized for the 4 CODEC edges of the I11 M0 diagram (enc_sol, enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1, dec_go): exactly 2,000 seeded grammar samples; every sort-boundary value of whitepaper §8.7 (each Header field at 0, 1, max and max - 1, and the version at every version sentinel of the facts, within the edge's domain; for Bytes inputs the lengths 0, 1 and every length sentinel, and the first byte at 0, 1, 254, 255 and every version sentinel; rule tests_m2/_i16.py::required_boundary); every REFUTED M0 witness of the edge's input sort in its domain; and each edge's refinement record compares exactly that corpus.

0 disagreements on every faithful edge, v2 inputs included (enc_go_v1 writes byte 0 = 1 exactly as Go does), and decoder domains included. Operationalized: every edge is treated as faithful. Each per-edge refinement record reports 0 disagreements and equal model and real output digests. That covers the 4 CODEC edges, each compared with its own implementation, plus the decoder domains ok_go (Go validate()) and ok_sol (Solidity _loadBatchHeader) on a Bytes corpus built by the same rule. The model digest equals the frozen reference interpreter's over the same corpus. Instruments fixed at the prereg reproduce every real digest: the Go instrument for enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1, dec_go and ok_go, the Foundry instrument for enc_sol and ok_sol. enc_go_v1's corpus holds version-2 grammar and boundary inputs, on which Go and the model both write byte 0 = 1. The dec_go, ok_go and ok_sol corpora hold inputs inside and outside their domains.

predictions.claim: O1 and O2 appear as cross-edge PAR differences linked to L_dom_hdr and L_par_hdr_v2, not in the refinement counts. Operationalized: results/M2/cross_edge.json holds a PAR difference between ok_go and ok_sol linked to L_dom_hdr, and one between enc_go_v1 and enc_sol linked to L_par_hdr_v2. Each linked law is REFUTED and its claim compares exactly that pair. Each recorded example satisfies the law's premises and differs under the reference interpreter (O2: byte 0 is 2 for enc_sol and 1 for enc_go_v1). The per-edge records of ok_go, ok_sol, enc_go_v1 and enc_sol count 0 disagreements, and no spec/M2/disagreements.json entry links either law.

0 unexplained. Operationalized: every entry of spec/M2/disagreements.json is classified from its links, by the rules fixed at the prereg (tests_m2/_i16.py::expected_class, which holon.refinement.classify matches), to a class other than unexplained, equal to its label. Every disagreement id that a refinement record lists has an entry. Gate check GREF passes on a copy of the committed tree.

Construction check, not counted toward prediction accuracy: the native build's outcome is recorded explicitly. results/M2/native.json has status native or fallback; a native status names the sha256 of the C source a fresh build emits, and the engine is an ELF binary under the build directory; a fallback carries a captured compiler error that a fresh build reproduces, and its refinement records run on .mjs. The C probe's recorded exit codes and output reproduce. The C driver is generated deterministically, without escape hatches.

Construction check, not counted: one refinement record per edge, against its own implementation, through the replay/M2 harnesses. Each record is pinned to the toolchain and the full morph commit, and harness dependencies stay outside the repo. The corpus is identical across processes and hash seeds. `holon refine --edges dec_go` reproduces the committed dec_go record byte for byte.

Construction check, not counted: the mechanical classes follow the links on the prereg fixture cases (tests_m2/fixtures/refinement/classifier_cases.json), whatever the label. GREF is a gate check, and it fails, naming the entry, on a mislabelled entry and on a disagreement that has no entry.

M1 refs are the M1 corpus per_action entries of the step_<a> definitions in the cone. Every ref resolves to a record with 0 disagreements.

Construction check, not counted: results/M0 and results/M1 metrics.json are deterministic, and their values follow the records, the gate report, the refinement records and the disagreements. Every other §13 metric is reported or listed under not_applicable. Timings, including from_scratch_gate_s, live only in metrics_timing.json. G1 compares metrics.json and excludes metrics_timing.json.
